title: License Key Formatting
spaceBreakdown:
- result string: this is the returned output, not counted as auxiliary space (LeetCode convention)
- reverse(): in-place on result, O(1) extra
- count, loop index i: O(1)
- not counted: input string s, returned result string
approach: Scan the input right-to-left, skipping dashes and uppercasing each alphanumeric character. Append characters to a result string, inserting a dash before every group of k characters (except before the very first character appended). Because we build from the end, every group except the last-built one - which becomes the first group after reversal - has exactly k characters. Finally, reverse the result in place. This avoids allocating an intermediate cleaned string, using only the output string itself.
hints: If the first group is allowed to be shorter than k, which end of the string should you start grouping from so that every group you form has a known, fixed size? The first group may be shorter than k but must contain at least one character.

Scan right-to-left, appending uppercased characters to a result string and inserting a dash every k characters, then reverse the result in place. For s = "5F3Z-2e-9-w", k = 4: scanning backward yields W,9,E,2,Z,3,F,5 → "W9E2-Z3F5" → reversed "5F3Z-2E9W".

```
count = 0
result = ""
for i from last index of s down to 0:
    if s[i] == '-': skip
    if count > 0 and count % k == 0:
        append '-' to result
    append uppercase(s[i]) to result
    count = count + 1
reverse result in place
return result
```

**Single character** - only one alphanumeric character, no dashes.
`Input: s = "a", k = 1` → `Expected: "A"`
⚠️ Bug: inserting a dash when `count % k == 0` without guarding `count > 0` → returns `"A-"`

**First group shorter** - total alphanumeric characters not divisible by k.
`Input: s = "abc", k = 2` → `Expected: "A-BC"`
⚠️ Bug: grouping left-to-right with the remainder in the last group → returns `"AB-C"`

**Lowercase letters** - input contains lowercase characters that must be uppercased.
`Input: s = "2-5g-3-J", k = 2` → `Expected: "2-5G-3J"`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the lowercase-to-uppercase conversion → returns `"2-5g-3J"`

**Exact multiple of k** - character count divides evenly, so no short first group.
`Input: s = "abcd", k = 4` → `Expected: "ABCD"`
⚠️ Bug: appending a dash after every k characters unconditionally, even at the end → returns `"-ABCD"`

followUps.q: What if the input arrives as a character stream too large to store in memory?
followUps.a: Make two passes over the stream: first count alphanumeric characters, then compute the first group size as count % k (or k if the remainder is 0). On the second pass, emit characters left-to-right, inserting a dash at each group boundary. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if each group must have a different size specified by an array k[0..m-1]?
followUps.a: First count alphanumeric characters and verify the total equals the sum of all k[i]. Then scan right-to-left, consuming k[m-1], k[m-2], …, k[0] characters per group and inserting dashes between groups. Time O(n), space O(1) extra beyond the given k array.

followUps.q: What if the separator is a multi-character string (e.g., "--") instead of a single dash?
followUps.a: Replace each `push_back('-')` with appending the separator string. The grouping logic is unchanged. Time O(n · separator_length) in the worst case, space O(1) extra.
